question: The control manifest declares ingress.staticBrandThemePath = "tokenOverrides". Does a value authored at BrandTheme.tokenOverrides reach the compiled CSS through compileBrandTheme?
answer: NO. BrandTheme.tokenOverrides (the raw --ds-* allowlist map the keypath names, contracts/composition/tenants/themes/index.ts:3331) is declared on the type but never read anywhere in the static compiler: zero property-access occurrences of `.tokenOverrides` in the whole of infrastructure/compilers/kernel/runtime/brand-theme/index.ts, and zero occurrences of `brandTheme.tokenOverrides` / `bt.tokenOverrides` / `theme.tokenOverrides` anywhere in production src/. The only slot the compiler DOES read under a similar name, BrandCompilerInput.verticalTokenOverrides (themes/index.ts:3378), is a SEPARATE compiler-input parameter carrying the VERTICAL's own baseline structural overrides (a different type, TenantTokenOverrides: surface/borderRadius/shadows/glass/gradients/overlays/densityScale/motion -- never a raw --ds-* map), supplied by whoever CALLS compileBrandTheme, not by BrandTheme itself. A stop that wrote there to make this control's static arm produce SOME movement would measure the wrong actor: the vertical re-authoring its own baseline, exactly the class H-1 closed.

The DB door (visualFoundation.advanced.tokenOverrides) was separately measured live via dist/server.js; see the receipted matrix in this same directory.
precision: DECLARED ON THE TYPE, NEVER CONSUMED -- stronger than responsive.posture's 'unreachable in a first-party vertical render' class. There the field was read by a real function (resolveActiveResponsivePosture) that a non-projected caller could still reach; here the read side does not exist in the compiler at all, for any caller, in any context. The type field is a promise the compiler never keeps.
consequence: A static-arm scenario for this control would do one of two things, both false witnesses. (a) Write to BrandTheme.tokenOverrides and measure zero-diff on every value, every channel, every vertical -- a control that never lowers through its declared static door is indistinguishable from a broken harness, and the CLI's own empty-lowering guard would have to be silenced to let it pass, hiding the defect rather than reporting it. (b) Write to verticalTokenOverrides and measure a DIFFERENT capability's territory (a vertical's own surface/motion baseline), attributing that movement to this control instead of to recipe-profile / surfaces.elevation-posture / motion.dial -- a false positive, not a false negative, and the more dangerous of the two because it would report success.
